  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and

    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR

    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io

    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open

# per file, NOT cat — a single shard's ratchet would see partial
  # lib/src/cli coverage and false-regress), then the CLI coverage ratchet
  # runs on the merged report, and the duration-budget gate (issue #928
  # Part 1) consumes the leg's three dart-json shard reports:
  # per-suite totals vs scripts/test_duration_baseline.json (down-only
  # ratchet, >10% suite regression or a per-test budget breach fails the
  # merge) and the top-10 slowest tests land in the job summary on every
  # run. The gate NEVER rewrites the baseline — budgets move only through
  # reviewed PRs running check_test_durations.py --update-baseline locally
  # against an integration-json artifact. gh-1005: the measurement
  # environment moved mac -> ubuntu-24.04-arm together with the leg (the
  # coverage-gardener already measured on ubuntu); a baseline re-seat, if
  # the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR
  # path.
  pty-coverage-gate:
    name: PTY gates (coverage ratchet + duration budget, merged shards)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [pty-integration-linux]
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      # gh-1300: issues: write — the duration-budget auto-filer files/
      # comments/closes the [ENH] optimization issue. A job-level
      # permissions block drops every unlisted scope to none, so both
      # scopes are listed explicitly (the filing leg reads nothing else).
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: pty-coverage-shard-*
          path: pty-coverage-shards
      # Same discipline as the core/faui shards' assert_shard_manifest: the 3
      # selections must cover exactly the integration-tagged suite
      # (browser-ext excluded, it owns browser-ext.yml), pairwise disjoint,
      # every unit on disk. Fails loudly BEFORE the ratchet reads shard data.
      - name: Assert integration shard manifest (union/disjoint/exists)
        run: python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm
      # The leg's dart json reports for the #928 duration gate below.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: integration-json-shard-*
          path: integration-json-shards
      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        run: |
          count=$(ls pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "3" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 3 pty shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          # gh-995: a report that downloads but carries no SF: records
          # (empty/truncated upload) still satisfies the count check and
          # merges into a silently partial report — the 2026-09-27 wedge
          # also showed the ratchet reading 7.95% vs the 11.00% baseline
          # off exactly such a merge. Fail loudly naming the hollow shard
          # instead of letting the ratchet chase a phantom regression.
          for f in pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info; do
            grep -q '^SF:' "$f" || { echo "::error::$f carries no SF: records — hollow shard coverage upload"; exit 1; }
          done
          mkdir -p coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py \
            -o coverage/lcov.merged.info \
            pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
      - name: CLI coverage ratchet (lib/src/cli/**, baseline only up)
        run: python3 scripts/check_cli_coverage.py --lcov coverage/lcov.merged.info
      - name: Test duration budget gate (issue #928, ratchet only down)
        run: |
          ls integration-json-shards/*
          python3 scripts/check_test_durations.py \
            --baseline scripts/test_duration_baseline.json \
            integration-json-shards/*/integration-shard-*.json
      # gh-1300: per-SHARD budget (expected runner span + headroom, one
      # place: scripts/test_shard_budgets.json). Breach fails the job
      # LOUDLY and writes the [ENH] issue body the filer step below posts
      # — crossing the line always produces work, never a silent bump.
      - name: Shard duration budget gate (gh-1300, down-only ratchet)
        id: shard_budget
        run: |
          python3 scripts/check_shard_durations.py \
            --budgets scripts/test_shard_budgets.json \
            --issue-body duration-budget-issue.md \
            --run-url "$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID" \
            integration-json-shards/*/integration-shard-*.json
      # Best-effort on forks (their GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write issues);
      # the gate failure above is the loud part. Deduped: an open
      # duration-budget issue is commented with the fresh numbers, not
      # duplicated (the nightly-red / flake-quarantine pattern).
      - name: File the duration-budget optimization issue (gh-1300)
        if: always() && steps.shard_budget.outcome == 'failure'
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          repo="$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          gh label create duration-budget --force \
            --description "PTY/CLI shard over its duration budget (gh-1300)" \
            --color D93F0B --repo "$repo"
          title="[ENH] PTY/CLI shard duration budget breach (auto-filed)"
          existing=$(gh issue list --state open --label duration-budget \
            --json number --jq '.[0].number' --repo "$repo")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --body-file duration-budget-issue.md \
              --repo "$repo"
          else
            gh issue create --title "$title" --label duration-budget \
              --body-file duration-budget-issue.md \
              --assignee ai-teammate --repo "$repo"
          fi
      # The auto-filed issue closes only when the run fits under the
      # budget again — the green path of THIS step is that proof.
      - name: Close the duration-budget issue on a fitting run
        if: always() && steps.shard_budget.outcome == 'success'
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          repo="$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          existing=$(gh issue list --state open --label duration-budget \
            --json number --jq '.[0].number' --repo "$repo")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" \
              --body "Fits under budget again: ${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${repo}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID} — closing."
            gh issue close "$existing" --repo "$repo"
          fi

  # gh-1005: Terminal visual is platform-independent and pinned to hosted
  # linux arm64. Evidence: every assertion reads the xterm terminal BUFFER /
  # screen text (never pixels — each PNG even ships a .txt twin "for
  # pixel-independent verification"), rendering goes through the BUNDLED
  # JetBrainsMono font (no host system fonts), and pty2 allocates the PTY
  # via libc openpty FFI. Nothing needs macOS — the old fa-m5 / macos-latest
  # routing (10x hosted-macOS minute cost, single-runner queue risk) is
  # gone; the nightly keeps an eyeball-only screenshot leg.
  pty-visual:
    name: Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 45

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1306
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1306
- **Title**: gh-1300 [ENH] PTY integration tests: pay toolchain+boot ONCE per shard, not per test (~30s spawn overhead × N tests) — boot-once + reset between tests (owner design), FA_BIN AOT seam as the cheap first cut
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1300` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 27
- **Additions**: +1609
- **Deletions**: -384
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T06:49:10Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T16:24:15Z

## PR Description

Closes #1300
### What changed
PTY/CLI integration tests now pay the toolchain once per CI run instead of once per test (gh-1300, FA_BIN-first cut): a new `fa-aot-build` job compiles `bin/fah.dart` to a native bundle ONCE per run (arm64, artifact relay), and every CLI spawn — the PTY harness (`FaCliHarness`) plus all 10 headless raw-spawn helpers — resolves through a new `faCliCommand()` seam that prefers `FA_BIN` (explicit env > ambient > original JIT shape). # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/S…

    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm

    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf

    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.

    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage

    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

blocks.text:
# per file, NOT cat — a single shard's ratchet would see partial
  # lib/src/cli coverage and false-regress), then the CLI coverage ratchet
  # runs on the merged report, and the duration-budget gate (issue #928
  # Part 1) consumes the leg's three dart-json shard reports:
  # per-suite totals vs scripts/test_duration_baseline.json (down-only
  # ratchet, >10% suite regression or a per-test budget breach fails the
  # merge) and the top-10 slowest tests land in the job summary on every
  # run. The gate NEVER rewrites the baseline — budgets move only through
  # reviewed PRs running check_test_durations.py --update-baseline locally
  # against an integration-json artifact. gh-1005: the measurement
  # environment moved mac -> ubuntu-24.04-arm together with the leg (the
  # coverage-gardener already measured on ubuntu); a baseline re-seat, if
  # the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR
  # path.
  pty-coverage-gate:
    name: PTY gates (coverage ratchet + duration budget, merged shards)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [pty-integration-linux]
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      # gh-1300: issues: write — the duration-budget auto-filer files/
      # comments/closes the [ENH] optimization issue. A job-level
      # permissions block drops every unlisted scope to none, so both
      # scopes are listed explicitly (the filing leg reads nothing else).
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: pty-coverage-shard-*
          path: pty-coverage-shards
      # Same discipline as the core/faui shards' assert_shard_manifest: the 3
      # selections must cover exactly the integration-tagged suite
      # (browser-ext excluded, it owns browser-ext.yml), pairwise disjoint,
      # every unit on disk. Fails loudly BEFORE the ratchet reads shard data.
      - name: Assert integration shard manifest (union/disjoint/exists)
        run: python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm
      # The leg's dart json reports for the #928 duration gate below.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: integration-json-shard-*
          path: integration-json-shards
      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        run: |
          count=$(ls pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "3" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 3 pty shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          # gh-995: a report that downloads but carries no SF: records
          # (empty/truncated upload) still satisfies the count check and
          # merges into a silently partial report — the 2026-09-27 wedge
          # also showed the ratchet reading 7.95% vs the 11.00% baseline
          # off exactly such a merge. Fail loudly naming the hollow shard
          # instead of letting the ratchet chase a phantom regression.
          for f in pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info; do
            grep -q '^SF:' "$f" || { echo "::error::$f carries no SF: records — hollow shard coverage upload"; exit 1; }
          done
          mkdir -p coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py \
            -o coverage/lcov.merged.info \
            pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
      - name: CLI coverage ratchet (lib/src/cli/**, baseline only up)
        run: python3 scripts/check_cli_coverage.py --lcov coverage/lcov.merged.info
      - name: Test duration budget gate (issue #928, ratchet only down)
        run: |
          ls integration-json-shards/*
          python3 scripts/check_test_durations.py \
            --baseline scripts/test_duration_baseline.json \
            integration-json-shards/*/integration-shard-*.json
      # gh-1300: per-SHARD budget (expected runner span + headroom, one
      # place: scripts/test_shard_budgets.json). Breach fails the job
      # LOUDLY and writes the [ENH] issue body the filer step below posts
      # — crossing the line always produces work, never a silent bump.
      - name: Shard duration budget gate (gh-1300, down-only ratchet)
        id: shard_budget
        run: |
          python3 scripts/check_shard_durations.py \
            --budgets scripts/test_shard_budgets.json \
            --issue-body duration-budget-issue.md \
            --run-url "$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID" \
            integration-json-shards/*/integration-shard-*.json
      # Best-effort on forks (their GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write issues);
      # the gate failure above is the loud part. Deduped: an open
      # duration-budget issue is commented with the fresh numbers, not
      # duplicated (the nightly-red / flake-quarantine pattern).
      - name: File the duration-budget optimization issue (gh-1300)
        if: always() && steps.shard_budget.outcome == 'failure'
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          repo="$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          gh label create duration-budget --force \
            --description "PTY/CLI shard over its duration budget (gh-1300)" \
            --color D93F0B --repo "$repo"
          title="[ENH] PTY/CLI shard duration budget breach (auto-filed)"
          existing=$(gh issue list --state open --label duration-budget \
            --json number --jq '.[0].number' --repo "$repo")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --body-file duration-budget-issue.md \
              --repo "$repo"
          else
            gh issue create --title "$title" --label duration-budget \
              --body-file duration-budget-issue.md \
              --assignee ai-teammate --repo "$repo"
          fi
      # The auto-filed issue closes only when the run fits under the
      # budget again — the green path of THIS step is that proof.
      - name: Close the duration-budget issue on a fitting run
        if: always() && steps.shard_budget.outcome == 'success'
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          repo="$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          existing=$(gh issue list --state open --label duration-budget \
            --json number --jq '.[0].number' --repo "$repo")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" \
              --body "Fits under budget again: ${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${repo}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID} — closing."
            gh issue close "$existing" --repo "$repo"
          fi

  # gh-1005: Terminal visual is platform-independent and pinned to hosted
  # linux arm64. Evidence: every assertion reads the xterm terminal BUFFER /
  # screen text (never pixels — each PNG even ships a .txt twin "for
  # pixel-independent verification"), rendering goes through the BUNDLED
  # JetBrainsMono font (no host system fonts), and pty2 allocates the PTY
  # via libc openpty FFI. Nothing needs macOS — the old fa-m5 / macos-latest
  # routing (10x hosted-macOS minute cost, single-runner queue risk) is
  # gone; the nightly keeps an eyeball-only screenshot leg.
  pty-visual:
    name: Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 45

===
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: dart pub get
      # gh-1300: compile the AOT bundle ONCE for the whole nightly leg and
      # point the FA_BIN seam at it — same shape as ci.yml's fa-aot-build
      # job (the nightly runs one unsharded job, so the build is in-job).
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - name: dart build cli (AOT bundle, gh-1300)
        run: |
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local
          version=$(sed -n 's/^version: //p' pubspec.yaml)
          echo "$version" > fa-local/bundle/version.txt
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (excluding browser-ext — it owns browser-ext.yml)
        # gh-1199 AC5/AC6: this unsharded leg (with secrets) is the
        # SUPERVISED home of the live (`llm`) suite — and it deliberately
        # does NOT apply the flake quarantine: a quarantined file keeps
        # running here nightly, producing the repeat-run proof its fix PR
        # needs for un-quarantine.
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn runs the AOT binary
          # (~1 s) instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on ARM).
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
        run: |
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration.json"
      # Issue #928 review: the file-reporter writes the json even on a RED
      # leg — convert + upload must not be chained into the failing step.
      # The RAW dart json is the machine-parseable form the gate itself
      # consumes (one format, both sides): a budget-tightening PR downloads
      # `integration-json` and runs check_test_durations.py --update-baseline
      # on it; junit stays for the human/rebalancer view.
      - name: junit durations (budget-tightening evidence)
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration.json
          test-results/junit-integration.xml
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json
          path: test-results/integration.json
          retention-days: 14

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/S…

    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open

    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed

blocks.text:
# per file, NOT cat — a single shard's ratchet would see partial
  # lib/src/cli coverage and false-regress), then the CLI coverage ratchet
  # runs on the merged report, and the duration-budget gate (issue #928
  # Part 1) consumes the leg's three dart-json shard reports:
  # per-suite totals vs scripts/test_duration_baseline.json (down-only
  # ratchet, >10% suite regression or a per-test budget breach fails the
  # merge) and the top-10 slowest tests land in the job summary on every
  # run. The gate NEVER rewrites the baseline — budgets move only through
  # reviewed PRs running check_test_durations.py --update-baseline locally
  # against an integration-json artifact. gh-1005: the measurement
  # environment moved mac -> ubuntu-24.04-arm together with the leg (the
  # coverage-gardener already measured on ubuntu); a baseline re-seat, if
  # the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR
  # path.
  pty-coverage-gate:
    name: PTY gates (coverage ratchet + duration budget, merged shards)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [pty-integration-linux]
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      # gh-1300: issues: write — the duration-budget auto-filer files/
      # comments/closes the [ENH] optimization issue. A job-level
      # permissions block drops every unlisted scope to none, so both
      # scopes are listed explicitly (the filing leg reads nothing else).
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: pty-coverage-shard-*
          path: pty-coverage-shards
      # Same discipline as the core/faui shards' assert_shard_manifest: the 3
      # selections must cover exactly the integration-tagged suite
      # (browser-ext excluded, it owns browser-ext.yml), pairwise disjoint,
      # every unit on disk. Fails loudly BEFORE the ratchet reads shard data.
      - name: Assert integration shard manifest (union/disjoint/exists)
        run: python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm
      # The leg's dart json reports for the #928 duration gate below.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: integration-json-shard-*
          path: integration-json-shards
      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        run: |
          count=$(ls pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "3" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 3 pty shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          # gh-995: a report that downloads but carries no SF: records
          # (empty/truncated upload) still satisfies the count check and
          # merges into a silently partial report — the 2026-09-27 wedge
          # also showed the ratchet reading 7.95% vs the 11.00% baseline
          # off exactly such a merge. Fail loudly naming the hollow shard
          # instead of letting the ratchet chase a phantom regression.
          for f in pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info; do
            grep -q '^SF:' "$f" || { echo "::error::$f carries no SF: records — hollow shard coverage upload"; exit 1; }
          done
          mkdir -p coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py \
            -o coverage/lcov.merged.info \
            pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
      - name: CLI coverage ratchet (lib/src/cli/**, baseline only up)
        run: python3 scripts/check_cli_coverage.py --lcov coverage/lcov.merged.info
      - name: Test duration budget gate (issue #928, ratchet only down)
        run: |
          ls integration-json-shards/*
          python3 scripts/check_test_durations.py \
            --baseline scripts/test_duration_baseline.json \
            integration-json-shards/*/integration-shard-*.json
      # gh-1300: per-SHARD budget (expected runner span + headroom, one
      # place: scripts/test_shard_budgets.json). Breach fails the job
      # LOUDLY and writes the [ENH] issue body the filer step below posts
      # — crossing the line always produces work, never a silent bump.
      - name: Shard duration budget gate (gh-1300, down-only ratchet)
        id: shard_budget
        run: |
          python3 scripts/check_shard_durations.py \
            --budgets scripts/test_shard_budgets.json \
            --issue-body duration-budget-issue.md \
            --run-url "$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID" \
            integration-json-shards/*/integration-shard-*.json
      # Best-effort on forks (their GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write issues);
      # the gate failure above is the loud part. Deduped: an open
      # duration-budget issue is commented with the fresh numbers, not
      # duplicated (the nightly-red / flake-quarantine pattern).
      - name: File the duration-budget optimization issue (gh-1300)
        if: always() && steps.shard_budget.outcome == 'failure'
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          repo="$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          gh label create duration-budget --force \
            --description "PTY/CLI shard over its duration budget (gh-1300)" \
            --color D93F0B --repo "$repo"
          title="[ENH] PTY/CLI shard duration budget breach (auto-filed)"
          existing=$(gh issue list --state open --label duration-budget \
            --json number --jq '.[0].number' --repo "$repo")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --body-file duration-budget-issue.md \
              --repo "$repo"
          else
            gh issue create --title "$title" --label duration-budget \
              --body-file duration-budget-issue.md \
              --assignee ai-teammate --repo "$repo"
          fi
      # The auto-filed issue closes only when the run fits under the
      # budget again — the green path of THIS step is that proof.
      - name: Close the duration-budget issue on a fitting run
        if: always() && steps.shard_budget.outcome == 'success'
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          repo="$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          existing=$(gh issue list --state open --label duration-budget \
            --json number --jq '.[0].number' --repo "$repo")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" \
              --body "Fits under budget again: ${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${repo}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID} — closing."
            gh issue close "$existing" --repo "$repo"
          fi

  # gh-1005: Terminal visual is platform-independent and pinned to hosted
  # linux arm64. Evidence: every assertion reads the xterm terminal BUFFER /
  # screen text (never pixels — each PNG even ships a .txt twin "for
  # pixel-independent verification"), rendering goes through the BUNDLED
  # JetBrainsMono font (no host system fonts), and pty2 allocates the PTY
  # via libc openpty FFI. Nothing needs macOS — the old fa-m5 / macos-latest
  # routing (10x hosted-macOS minute cost, single-runner queue risk) is
  # gone; the nightly keeps an eyeball-only screenshot leg.
  pty-visual:
    name: Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 45

The gate job looks well-formed. Notes:

    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm

    env:

      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: dart pub get
      # gh-1300: compile the AOT bundle ONCE for the whole nightly leg and
      # point the FA_BIN seam at it — same shape as ci.yml's fa-aot-build
      # job (the nightly runs one unsharded job, so the build is in-job).
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - name: dart build cli (AOT bundle, gh-1300)
        run: |
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local
          version=$(sed -n 's/^version: //p' pubspec.yaml)
          echo "$version" > fa-local/bundle/version.txt
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah

      - name: dart test --tags integration (excluding browser-ext — it owns browser-ext.yml)
        # gh-1199 AC5/AC6: this unsharded leg (with secrets) is the

        # running here nightly, producing the repeat-run proof its fix PR

with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1300` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 27
- **Additions**: +1609
- **Deletions**: -384
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T06:49:10Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T16:24:15Z

## PR Description

Closes #1300
### What changed
PTY/CLI integration tests now pay the toolchain once per CI run instead of once per test (gh-1300, FA_BIN-first cut): a new `fa-aot-build` job compiles `bin/fah.dart` to a native bundle ONCE per run (arm64, artifact relay), and every CLI spawn — the PTY harness (`FaCliHarness`) plus all 10 headless raw-spawn helpers — resolves through a new `faCliCommand()` seam that prefers `FA_BIN` (explicit env > ambient > original JIT shape). A new per-shard duration-budget ratchet (`scripts/check_shard_durations.py` + `scripts/test_shard_budgets.json`, self-tested in the guards leg) fails the gate on breach and auto-files/updates/closes a deduped `[ENH]` `duration-budget` issue with measured-vs-budget numbers.

### Key decisions
- FA_BIN first (ticket's sanctioned cheap cut), boot-once+reset left as follow-up: zero isolation redesign, per-test isolation contract documented on `FaCliHarness` (AC5 — session/config/keys/mailboxes/secrets/screen/turn-grants/shell-jobs reset by fresh-process construction; #948 unique-cwd rule preserved)
- Binary is built fresh from the PR's sources every run (never cached across runs); shards smoke it (`test -x` + `--version`) and fail loudly — no silent JIT fallback; `fa-aot-build` failure fails the Quality gate (skipped-shard dodge closed)
- Budget = expected runner span + headroom, pinned in ONE file; down-only ratchet (`--update-budgets` refuses raises); seeded 420 s/shard pre-seam, to be tightened from this PR's artifacts
- AC3: the 5 boot band-aids (`waitForBoot` 300 s/5 min) removed back to the 90 s default — the CFE-compile race is gone

### Measured (AC1; CI before/after lands via this run's junit artifacts)
- per-spawn: `dart bin/fah.dart --version` 8.6–8.7 s (JIT, warm) → AOT binary < 0.01 s (CI JIT ≈ 28–32 s/test per the ticket evidence)
- per-file E2E (composer_echo, local): 39 s → 20 s; gate summary prints the measured-vs-budget table per shard
- incidental: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` self-version re-synced (1.0.514 → 1.0.515) — main's release commit left it stale and `nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test` AC2 caught it

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/integration/pty_harness_fa_bin_test.dart   # seam unit tests
bash scripts/duration_budget_selftest.sh                  # gate self-test (AC6: breach→FAIL+issue body)
dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local && echo "$(sed -n 's/^version: //p' pubspec.yaml)" > fa-local/bundle/version.txt
FA_BIN=$PWD/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah dart test --tags integration   # full suite on AOT
```
Locally proven: seam suite green, 8 PTY files × 3 randomized repeats green, converted headless suites (`backend_mode`, `headless_log_file`, `ctrl_c`, `dap_cli_e2e`, `poisoned_provider`) green on AOT, JIT fallback (no FA_BIN) green, flutter cli_visual harness tests 14/14.

  S -->|FA_BIN env| H[faCliCommand seam: harness + headless helpers]

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through

  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# duration_budget_selftest.sh — fixture self-test for the gh-1300 shard
+# duration-budget gate (check_shard_durations.py).
+#
+# Proves, on fabricated dart-json reports (no CI, no real shards):
+#   AC1 a breaching shard FAILS the gate (exit 1) and the issue body
+#       carries measured-vs-budget numbers + the slowest-tests table;
+#   AC2 a fitting shard passes (exit 0) and writes no issue body;
+#   AC3 the warn band (>= warn_fraction of budget) passes but warns
+#       loudly in the summary;
+#   AC4 an unbudgeted shard is a loud failure (a new shard cannot sneak
+#       past the ratchet);
+#   AC5 --update-budgets is down-only: it lowers and adds, refuses to
+#       raise.
+# Same discipline as check_lockfiles_selftest.sh (#1100 pattern): the
+# gate's own red exits are fixture-tested so the check cannot rot
+# silently.
+set -u
+HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
+GATE="$HERE/check_shard_durations.py"
+TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
+trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
+
+fails=0
+check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
+  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
+    echo "  ok: $1"
+  else
+    echo "  FAIL: $1"
+    fails=$((fails + 1))
+  fi
+}
+check_fail() { # check_fail <desc> <exit-code: non-zero = pass>
+  if [ "$2" != "0" ]; then
+    echo "  ok: $1"
+  else
+    echo "  FAIL: $1"
+    fails=$((fails + 1))
+  fi
+}
+
+# ── fixture: one dart-json shard report with two sequential tests ────────
+# 90 s wall (100 ms → 90_100 ms): "slow case" 60 s + "quick case" 30 s.
+make_report() { # make_report <path>
+  cat >"$1" <<'EOF'
+{"type":"suite","suite":{"id":1,"path":"test/integration/slow_suite_test.dart","platform":"vm"}}
+{"type":"suite","suite":{"id":2,"path":"test/integration/quick_suite_test.dart","platform":"vm"}}
+{"type":"testStart","test":{"id":10,"name":"slow case","suiteID":1},"time":100}
+{"type":"testDone","testID":10,"result":"success","hidden":false,"time":60100}
+{"type":"testStart","test":{"id":11,"name":"quick case","suiteID":2},"time":60100}
+{"type":"testDone","testID":11,"result":"success","hidden":false,"time":90100}
+EOF
+}
+
+python3 - "$GATE" <<'EOF' || { echo "FAIL: $GATE missing"; exit 1; }
+import os, sys
+sys.exit(0 if os.path.isfile(sys.argv[1]) else 1)
+EOF
+[ $? = 0 ] || { echo "gate script missing — self-test cannot run"; exit 1; }
+
+budgets0="$TMP/budgets0.json"

+

**A. faCliCommand precedence** — explicit faBin (extraEnv) > ambient FA_BIN env > JIT. In `FaCliHarness.spawn`, env is built with whitelist + extraEnv. Note: previously, `faBin = extraEnv?['FA_BIN']` — only explicit extraEnv FA_BIN was honored. Now ambient `Platform.environment['FA_BIN']` is also honored. Is there any risk that a developer's environment has FA_BIN set to something stale? Documented behavior; tests use temp HOME, but FA_BIN points at a binary. It's a test-only seam — acceptable. But one subtle issue: when FA_BIN is set and `vmServicePort != null`, the VM flags are dropped silently (the AOT binary has no VM service). Previously with explicit faBin, the same behavior existed (flags only included when faBin == null). Now ambient FA_BIN also drops them. Does any test use vmServicePort? Let me grep.

**B. `dap_wake_hang_test.dart` pgrep pattern** — `Platform.environment['FA_BIN'] ?? 'bin/fah.dart'` — pgrep -f with full path containing slashes; pgrep -f pattern is a regex — a path contains `/` which is fine in regex, but also `.` matches any char (fine, broadens). Minor. Also if FA_BIN is relative... it's absolute in CI. OK. Minor note: pattern is used in `ps` too? It prints message. Fine.

**C. The removed prewarm step in ci.yml** — the "Prewarm build hooks + fa boot" step was replaced by download + chmod + smoke. The comment in the old step said the warm cache is needed so the duration gate measures warm-boot truth. Now shards still have the hooks cache restored (the cache step remains — "Same hooks cache key as the shards: the build pays the native assets hooks here so the shard-side restore is warm"). OK.

But wait — do the shards still need `dart pub get`? Yes presumably unchanged.

If the shards use a different Dart version (e.g. flutter's dart or a pinned version), the AOT snapshot built by a different SDK version could be incompatible? AOT native executables are self-contained (include their own Dart runtime), so SDK version mismatch matters only for... actually a native AOT executable bundles the runtime, so it runs regardless of the shards' SDK. But the native-assets hooks: the binary embeds native assets built in the build job (sqlite3 FFI). The build job runs `dart pub get` with sdk stable — the pubspec may pin an SDK constraint; the shards use some setup — let me check what setup-dart version ci.yml shards use. If build job uses `stable` while the repo pins a specific version elsewhere, there could be drift: e.g., CI elsewhere uses a specific SDK, and `dart build` with a NEWER stable could produce different behavior. Let me check the workflow for what SDK the other jobs use.

  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the

  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only

    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart
